map.text: decompile.py parses source into cells, lifts them through layers via Bedrock, checks and numbers the tree, resolves cross-references with Jedi, and writes map.json.

children.text: imports, PROMPT, and the core functions parse source into cells, send prompts to Bedrock, validate groups, and build tree nodes.
imports, PROMPT, statements(), cells_of(), merge(), and ask() load tools, define the prompt, parse source into cells, and send prompts to Bedrock.
imports, PROMPT, statements(), and cells_of() load tools, define the prompt, and parse the source into statement ranges and cell spans.
imports and PROMPT load the tools and instruct the model on how to merge cells into labeled groups.
imports bring in the tools: ast, json, os, sys, pathlib, boto3, jedi, botocore Config, and dotenv, then load_dotenv() reads the credentials from the .env file next to the script.
imports bring in the tools: ast, json, os, sys, pathlib, boto3, jedi, botocore Config, and dotenv.
load_dotenv() reads the credentials from the .env file next to the script.
PROMPT instructs the model to merge code cells into labeled groups with one plain-English sentence each, following rules for size, coverage, and voice.
statements() and cells_of() parse the source AST to produce statement ranges and cell spans.
statements() parses the source, walks the AST, and returns depth and line range for every statement node.
statements() returns early for non-Python files and initializes the rows list.
statements()'s walk() recurses the AST and appends depth, start line, and end line for each statement node.
statements() calls walk() on the parsed source and returns the rows.
cells_of() splits the source into cell spans by walking the AST, then fills gaps and returns sorted cell dicts.
cells_of() sets up the spans list and checks the file suffix.
cells_of()'s kids_of() collects direct statement children of an AST node, recursing into non-statement nodes.
cells_of()'s emit() handles a leaf node by appending its line range to spans.
cells_of()'s emit() builds covered and recurses into each child statement.
cells_of()'s emit() collects the node's own non-covered lines into spans.
cells_of() calls emit() on every top-level AST node in src.
cells_of()'s fallback stage groups non-blank lines into spans when no AST spans were found, then returns them.
cells_of() finds lines not covered by any span and collects them into extra.
cells_of() merges each extra run into the nearest following span, or into the last span.
cells_of() returns all spans sorted and wrapped as cell dicts.
merge() and ask() combine overlapping spans and send the prompt to Bedrock, then return the parsed JSON reply.
merge() joins overlapping or adjacent line spans into a sorted, non-overlapping list.
ask() sends the prompt to the Bedrock model and returns the parsed JSON from the reply.
check_pass() and lift() validate the model's groups and build the next layer of tree nodes.
check_pass() checks that the groups list is valid: count went down, each group starts at the right cell, text is non-empty, size is at most 15 lines on a first pass, and no group cuts a statement.
check_pass() gets the groups list and checks that it is a non-empty list and that the count went down.
check_pass()'s loop checks that each group starts at the right cell, ends in range, and has a non-empty text.
check_pass()'s loop collects non-blank lines for the group and checks that the count is at most 15 on a first pass.
check_pass()'s loop checks that no group cuts a statement across its boundary.
check_pass()'s loop advances at to the next cell after the group.
check_pass() asserts all cells are covered and returns the groups list.
lift() turns a list of groups into tree nodes, keeps single-text cells as-is, and attaches children when kids already have text.
tree utilities and main() walk nodes, assign ids, map lines to owners, find references, write map.json, and drive the lift loop.
nodes_of(), number(), owner_of(), links(), row_of(), write_node(), and write_map() walk the tree, assign ids, map lines to nodes, find name references, and write map.json.
nodes_of(), number(), and owner_of() walk the tree to list all nodes, assign T-prefixed ids, and map each line to its leaf id.
nodes_of() walks the tree and returns every node in order, including children.
number() assigns a T-prefixed id to every node in the tree.
owner_of() maps each line number to the id of the leaf node that covers it.
links(), row_of(), write_node(), and write_map() find in-file name references, format cell strings, and write the file name, links, and map to map.json.
links() and row_of() find in-file name references with jedi and format each cell as a display string.
links() finds all in-file name references with jedi and returns each name with its def node and used nodes.
links() returns early if the file is not a .py file.
links() resolves the path, builds a jedi Script, and prepares the output list.
links() loops over names, skips external definitions and unmapped lines, finds all in-file references, and appends each name with its def node and used nodes.
links() returns the finished rows list.
row_of() builds a display string for a cell: its index, its line spans, and its text or first code line.
write_node() and write_map() serialize the tree nodes and write the file name, links, and map to map.json.
write_node() formats one tree node as a JSON string, with indented children if it has any.
write_map() writes the file name, links, and map tree to map.json as formatted JSON.
top_chunks(), one_pass(), and main() split cells at big-statement boundaries, lift chunks up to 8 times, then number the tree and write map.json.
top_chunks() and one_pass() split cells at big-statement boundaries and ask the model up to 8 times to lift each chunk.
top_chunks() groups cells into chunks, splitting only at boundaries between big top-level statements.
top_chunks() builds the list of tops and marks which ones are big.
top_of() finds the top-level statement that owns a cell.
top_chunks() groups cells into chunks, splitting only at big top-level boundaries.
one_pass() asks the model up to 8 times, checks each reply, returns the lifted groups on success, and exits on failure.
one_pass() sets up the prompt rows, the base prompt, and the retry state.
one_pass() asks the model up to 8 times, checks each reply, and returns the lifted groups on success.
one_pass() exits the program when all 8 attempts fail.
main() reads the source, builds cells and statement data, runs one_pass() until one root remains, then numbers the tree and writes map.json.
main()'s first stage reads the source file, builds cells, stmts, blank, ess, and stext.
main() opens the input file, splits it into lines, and checks it is not empty.
main() reads the source file, splits it into lines, checks it is not empty, and builds the numbered code string.
main() builds cells, stmts, and the blank-line set from the source.
main() builds ess: the set of non-blank lines that belong to leaf statements only.
main() builds stext: the statement-range block that the prompt sends to the model.
main()'s second stage runs one_pass() until one root cell remains, then numbers the tree and writes map.json.
main() runs one_pass() in a loop, splitting by top-level chunk on the first pass, until one root cell with a text remains.
main() numbers the tree, finds cross-reference links, and writes map.json.
main() runs when the script starts directly.
